name: Comoros
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. IDs are TL:<subject>:<measure>:<vintage> and stable across builds: a changed value under the same ID is an upstream revision (recorded in the ledger at /ledger); a new observed year is a new claim. A null or absent figure mints no claim — absence is never zero. Scheme: https://terralore.co/integrity

claims.title: Earliest settlement of the islands
claims.summary: Austronesian seafarers and Bantu-speaking peoples from the African mainland settle the archipelago, occupying the islands no later than the eighth century CE and embedding them in Swahili-coast networks.

sources.label: A history of Grande Comore (Ngazidja) ca. 700–1900

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-700-earliest-settlement-of-the-islands, claim TL:COM:event:700:earliest-settlement-of-the-islands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dembeni phase and Indian Ocean trade
claims.summary: The Dembeni-phase settlement flourishes as one of the richest sites of its age in the region, trading rock crystal and other goods with the Abbasid and Fatimid worlds and importing Persian and Chinese ceramics.

sources.label: Islamic Archaeology in the Comoros: The Swahili and the Rock Crystal Trade with the Abbasid and Fatimid Caliphates

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-900-dembeni-phase-and-indian-ocean-trade, claim TL:COM:event:900:dembeni-phase-and-indian-ocean-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Islam takes root
claims.summary: Islam, carried by Indian Ocean merchants and migrants, becomes established across the islands, tying the Comoros to the religious culture of the Swahili coast.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1100-islam-takes-root, claim TL:COM:event:1100:islam-takes-root, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the island sultanates
claims.summary: Muslim sultanates of Swahili culture emerge on the islands, with ruling houses claiming Arab, Persian (Shirazi) and Hadhrami descent to legitimise their authority.

sources.label: A history of Grande Comore (Ngazidja) ca. 700–1900

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1500-rise-of-the-island-sultanates, claim TL:COM:event:1500:rise-of-the-island-sultanates, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Portuguese and European contact
claims.summary: Portuguese navigators reach the islands in the early sixteenth century; the Comoros become a provisioning station for ships crossing the western Indian Ocean.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1505-portuguese-and-european-contact, claim TL:COM:event:1505:portuguese-and-european-contact, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Malagasy slaving raids
claims.summary: Sakalava and Betsimisaraka war-fleets from Madagascar raid the Comoros for captives over several decades, devastating communities across the archipelago.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1785-malagasy-slaving-raids, claim TL:COM:event:1785:malagasy-slaving-raids, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Slave society on the islands
claims.summary: The slave trade and plantation labour expand greatly, and by the mid-nineteenth century enslaved people are estimated to make up a very large proportion of the islands' population.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1860-slave-society-on-the-islands, claim TL:COM:event:1860:slave-society-on-the-islands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mayotte ceded to France
claims.summary: The ruler of Mayotte cedes the island to France, giving France its first foothold in the Comoro archipelago.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1841-mayotte-ceded-to-france, claim TL:COM:event:1841:mayotte-ceded-to-france, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Protectorates over the three islands
claims.summary: France establishes protectorates over Grande Comore, Anjouan and Mohéli, dealing with sultans including Said Ali bin Said Omar of Grande Comore.

sources.label: Said Ali bin Said Omar of Grande Comore

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1886-protectorates-over-the-three-islands, claim TL:COM:event:1886:protectorates-over-the-three-islands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Annexation and administration via Madagascar
claims.summary: The islands are formally brought under French possession and attached to the colony of Madagascar; the last sultan relinquishes power by 1912.

sources.label: Said Ali bin Said Omar of Grande Comore

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1908-annexation-and-administration-via-madagascar, claim TL:COM:event:1908:annexation-and-administration-via-madagascar, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Plantation economy
claims.summary: Colonial rule reorganises the economy around export crops—vanilla, cloves, copra and especially ylang-ylang—making the Comoros a leading supplier of perfume essence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1900-plantation-economy, claim TL:COM:event:1900:plantation-economy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Separate overseas territory
claims.summary: The Comoros are detached from Madagascar and constituted as a distinct French overseas territory, beginning to acquire their own institutions.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1946-separate-overseas-territory, claim TL:COM:event:1946:separate-overseas-territory, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Overseas territory with representation
claims.summary: The Comoros are confirmed as a French overseas territory and given representation in the French Parliament and a local assembly.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1947-overseas-territory-with-representation, claim TL:COM:event:1947:overseas-territory-with-representation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Internal autonomy granted
claims.summary: A year after Madagascar's independence, the Comoros are granted internal autonomy, with their own governing council and capital at Moroni.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1961-internal-autonomy-granted, claim TL:COM:event:1961:internal-autonomy-granted, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence referendum
claims.summary: Voters back independence by about 95 per cent across the archipelago, but on Mayotte a majority of roughly 63 per cent votes to remain French, splitting the islands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1974-independence-referendum, claim TL:COM:event:1974:independence-referendum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Unilateral declaration of independence
claims.summary: The Chamber of Deputies in Moroni, led by Ahmed Abdallah, declares the Comoros independent, claiming all four islands; Abdallah becomes first president.

sources.label: The Comoros declared an Independent State

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1975-unilateral-declaration-of-independence, claim TL:COM:event:1975:unilateral-declaration-of-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Admitted to the United Nations
claims.summary: The Comoros joins the UN under General Assembly resolution 3385 (XXX), which reaffirms the territorial integrity of the archipelago including Mayotte.

sources.label: The Franco-Comorian Territorial Dispute on Mayotte

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1975-admitted-to-the-united-nations, claim TL:COM:event:1975:admitted-to-the-united-nations, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Abdallah overthrown
claims.summary: A coalition aided by mercenaries led by Bob Denard ousts President Ahmed Abdallah weeks after independence, beginning a long era of coups.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1975-abdallah-overthrown, claim TL:COM:event:1975:abdallah-overthrown, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ali Soilih's revolution
claims.summary: Radical leftist Ali Soilih takes power and launches a confrontational revolution against the sultans, religious notables and old order, alienating France and the elite.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1976-ali-soilih-s-revolution, claim TL:COM:event:1976:ali-soilih-s-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Denard restores Abdallah
claims.summary: Bob Denard returns with mercenaries, overthrows Soilih—who is soon killed—and restores Ahmed Abdallah; the state becomes the Federal Islamic Republic of the Comoros.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1978-denard-restores-abdallah, claim TL:COM:event:1978:denard-restores-abdallah, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assassination of Ahmed Abdallah
claims.summary: President Abdallah is shot dead in his office in Moroni in disputed circumstances; Denard is widely suspected but later acquitted, and is pressured to leave.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1989-assassination-of-ahmed-abdallah, claim TL:COM:event:1989:assassination-of-ahmed-abdallah, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Operation Kaskari and French intervention
claims.summary: Bob Denard seizes Moroni with mercenaries in his final coup attempt; France intervenes in 'Operation Azalée' and removes him within days.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1995-operation-kaskari-and-french-intervention, claim TL:COM:event:1995:operation-kaskari-and-french-intervention, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Anjouan and Mohéli secede
claims.summary: Anjouan and Mohéli declare separation from the Comoros; a federal attempt to retake Anjouan by force is defeated, pushing the archipelago towards fragmentation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1997-anjouan-and-moheli-secede, claim TL:COM:event:1997:anjouan-and-moheli-secede, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Azali Assoumani seizes power
claims.summary: Army chief Azali Assoumani takes power in a coup amid the secession crisis, casting himself as the guarantor of national unity.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1999-azali-assoumani-seizes-power, claim TL:COM:event:1999:azali-assoumani-seizes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Union constitution and rotating presidency
claims.summary: Following the Fomboni accords, a new constitution approved by referendum creates the Union of the Comoros, giving each island autonomy and rotating the Union presidency among the three islands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-2001-union-constitution-and-rotating-presidency, claim TL:COM:event:2001:union-constitution-and-rotating-presidency, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mayotte votes to become a French department
claims.summary: In a referendum, Mayotte votes overwhelmingly to become a fully integrated French department, a status it assumes in 2011 as France's 101st department.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-2009-mayotte-votes-to-become-a-french-department, claim TL:COM:event:2009:mayotte-votes-to-become-a-french-department, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: UN affirms Comorian sovereignty over Mayotte
claims.summary: The UN General Assembly has repeatedly affirmed Comorian sovereignty over Mayotte and the archipelago's territorial integrity; the Comoros claims the island while France administers it.

sources.label: The Franco-Comorian Territorial Dispute on Mayotte
Question of the Comorian island of Mayotte (UN General Assembly resolution)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Comoros: An Indian Ocean archipelago of Swahili-Muslim sultanates, drawn into the spice and slave trades, colonised by France, and independent since 1975 amid coups, secessions and an unresolved dispute over Mayotte.", terralore.co/country/COM/chronicle#ev-1976-un-affirms-comorian-sovereignty-over-mayotte, claim TL:COM:event:1976:un-affirms-comorian-sovereignty-over-mayotte, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The medinas of the sultanates inscribed
claims.summary: The Medinas of the Historic Sultanates of the Comoros become the archipelago's first World Heritage site — the stone towns of the pre-colonial sultanates recognised on criteria (iii) and (iv).

sources.label: The Medinas of the Historic Sultanates of the Comoros (World Heritage List)
